title: Christmas Kaomoji *<|:-): Copy & Paste Festive Text Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste Christmas kaomoji: Santa *<|:-), reindeer Ψ(•ᴥ•)Ψ, snowy faces ｡ﾟ❄ﾟ｡(*´▽`*)｡ﾟ❄ﾟ｡, shivering (((>_<))) and faces handing over a gift 🎁.
hero_tagline: Santa, reindeer, snowmen and gift-giving faces in plain text for cards, captions and December chats. One tap copies a face.
intro: Christmas kaomoji mix Japanese text faces with a few seasonal characters. ❄ (U+2744) scatters snow around a face, ☃ (U+2603) is a text snowman, and Ψ, the Greek capital psi, sits on both sides of a face like a pair of antlers to make a reindeer. Santa is older than kaomoji: *<|:-) is a Western sideways emoticon where *<| is the hat with its bobble. Most of these get sent from early December through Christmas Day on 25 December, and the snow and shivering faces keep working all winter. The emoji side of the season, 🎄 🎅 🎁 and the rest, is on the Christmas symbols page linked below.

sections.label: Reindeer
sections.intro: Ψ on each side draws the antlers, and ᴥ is the snout. Swap the nose for ◉ to get Rudolph.

sections.label: Snow & Snowmen
sections.intro: ❄ falls around the face and ☃ stands next to it. These suit any cold day, not only Christmas.

sections.label: Gifts & Trees
sections.intro: Faces handing over a present or standing by the tree, for thank-you messages and gift photos.

faq.a: It is Santa Claus as a sideways Western emoticon. Tilt your head left: *<| is the pointed hat with its bobble, : is the eyes, the hyphen is the nose and ) is the smile. Swap ) for D and he is laughing.

faq.q: How do I make a reindeer kaomoji?
faq.a: Put Ψ, the Greek capital letter psi, on both sides of a face with an animal snout, as in Ψ(•ᴥ•)Ψ. Its three prongs look like antlers. For Rudolph, replace the snout with a filled circle such as ◉.

faq.q: Which snowflake character is used in these faces?
faq.a: ❄, U+2744 SNOWFLAKE from the Dingbats block. Many phones show it in color as the snowflake emoji. The text snowman ☃ is U+2603, a separate character from the ⛄ emoji.
